rationale: Lycopolitan compound: ⲣⲙ̄- ('man of') + ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ (Lyc. variant of ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ 'new,' confirmed in accumulated vocabulary entry 'ⲣⲙⲉⲉ → new'). Pauline καινὸς ἄνθρωπος (Eph 4:24, Col 3:10), adapted in Manichaean anthropology as the redeemed self whose five faculties produce virtues. Antithesis with ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲉⲥ ('Old Man') in this kephalaion confirms the reading.

Compound ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ϯ- ('give') + ⲛⲁϣⲧⲉ ('strength, hardness'). Standard agent-noun formation paralleling ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher' (already in glossary). Co-occurs with ⲣⲉϩⲥⲁⲛⲉϣ 'nourisher' as a pair of nurturing/sustaining roles.

Lyc. ⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ — variant of ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ ('purpose of heart') already in accumulated vocabulary. With possessive prefix ⲡⲉϩ- 'his.' May denote the inclination/wish that the indwelling Mind of Light fulfills in the New Man.

Abstract noun ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲥⲉⲃⲉ. The form is the antonym of ⲥⲃⲱ ('teaching') in this kephalaion's binary structure — but here ⲥⲉⲃⲉ functions as the privative/corrupt counterpart, hence 'foolishness' (Sah. ⲥⲟϭ 'fool'?). The Old Man's five members are characterized by ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲉⲃⲉ in line 17, parallel to the New Man's wisdom.
Abstract: ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲍⲏⲧ ('heart') + ⲥⲛⲉⲩ ('two') = 'state of two-heartedness' = δίψυχος (cf. James 1:8). The state into which Sin throws the Old Man by breaking his unity-of-heart.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'to add, place upon.' With ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧⲥ̄ 'within it' = 'add into.' Used here of the New Man adding his speech upon the purified image.
